title: Log analysis
summary: Read access and auth logs with standard text tools and spot scanning and password guessing.

steps.title: The logs
body: Split on spaces: `$1` client IP, `$4` time, `$6 $7` method and path, `$9` status, `$10` size.
Nov 20 15:02:11 web sshd[40012]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 185.12.3.4 port 51234 ssh2
Nov 20 15:04:40 web sshd[40999]: Accepted password for backup from 185.12.3.4 port 50001 ssh2
`invalid user` = the account doesn't exist; plain `Failed password for X` = it does.

steps.prompt: What does `awk '{print $9}'` print for this access log line?

steps.title: The toolkit
body: grep 'text' file / grep -v 'text' file   # lines with / without text
grep -o 'from [0-9.]*' file              # only the matching part
awk '$9 == 404 {print $1}' file          # field 1 where field 9 is 404
sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head         # count identical lines, most frequent first
The most useful line in log analysis, "which IP made the most requests?":
awk '{print $1}' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
> **Try it for real:** the live lab *Log analysis: spotting an incident* on the Labs page (needs Docker).

steps.prompt: Complete the pipeline: the IPs with the most **failed** SSH passwords.
code: grep 'Failed password' auth.log | grep -o 'from [0-9.]*' | __1__ | uniq __2__ | sort __3__ | head
steps.explain: `uniq -c` only counts *adjacent* duplicates, so sort first.

steps.prompt: Match each pattern to what it suggests.
pairs: One IP, many different paths, mostly 404, seconds apart
Many `Failed password` for many usernames, one IP
`Accepted password` right after many failures from that IP

items: A visitor hits one 404 on an old link
A few 401s at 9am as people log in
300 404s in a minute from one IP
`GET /wp-login.php` on a site that isn't WordPress
Login success for `backup` from an overseas IP

steps.prompt: You found `Accepted password for backup from 185.12.3.4` after 400 failures from the same IP. What comes first?
options: Contain: disable the `backup` account / kill its sessions and block the IP, then scope what it did
Delete the log so nobody panics
Wait to see if it happens again
steps.explain: Notice, scope, contain, fix the root cause (here: password login, fixed in the next lesson).

steps.title: Top talkers
prompt: Write `List<string> Top(List<string> accessLines, int n)` returning the `n` most frequent client IPs (field 1) formatted like `uniq -c` would after `sort -rn`:
template: Dojo.Eq("ties by IP", new List<string> { "2 10.0.0.2", "1 10.0.0.1", "1 10.0.0.3" }, Top(dojoL.Take(4).ToList(), 5));

steps.title: Spot scanners
prompt: Write `List<string> Scanners(List<string> accessLines, int threshold)` returning, sorted ordinally, the IPs that got a `404` on at least `threshold` **distinct** paths.
Path is field 7, status field 9 (split on single spaces).
template: Dojo.Eq("typo repeated is one path", new List<string> { "10.17.1.31", "185.12.3.4" }, Scanners(dojoL, 1));
hints: Fields are zero-based in C#: path is `f[6]`, status `f[8]`.
